purpose: Compare the first common bound-0 BVE schedule entering the per-candidate H lifecycle on Rank 17, using a one-row target observer that exits before any candidate is processed.

observer.interpretation: The symmetric bve_schedule payload records scheduled count, external-variable set hashes, insertion order, physical heap topology, and score-set hashes before the first candidate mutation.

attempts.result: Neither arm reached a BVE schedule in 300 seconds; both retained traces contain only headers. Tactix recorded a clean timeout. Kissat reached the same subprocess timeout but then exposed a bytes-to-JSON serialization bug in the observer harness. Temporary solver data was already removed by the context manager; no result is scored.

After the bytes/JSON repair, both arms again reached the 900-second cap without a BVE schedule row. Both traces are the identical 202-byte header and every task-local artifact was deleted. Kissat remained in instrumented preprocessing at 867 seconds. Global event instrumentation is therefore unsuitable for this boundary; do not retry it. Replace it with a standalone one-row BVE-schedule observer that does not activate global event tracing.

validation_contract: Both arms must hash-check their immutable binary and exact input, exit zero only on exactly one selected bound-0 schedule row, and delete all task-local solver data. This observer intentionally does not produce a SAT/UNSAT verdict and is not scored.
n1_n4: No source or production behavior changes; no rank/formula/benchmark selector; no effort/admission/classification change; historical immutable trace binaries only.
